requirements.implementation_scope: Actual finite structural role graph worklist and full supplied raw-axiom closure. Exact byte identity/orientation, duplicates, cycles and first forbidden required occurrence are covered. The raw collector is proved to supply every reached node; missing-node outcomes are impossible at the raw entry points. Only the simple-role restriction is decided. Imported closure assembly, chain regularity, datatype/anonymous/global restrictions and full DL validation remain separate.

requirements.requirement: RoleHierarchyRegularity
requirements.implementation_scope: Full raw-axiom property-hierarchy regularity condition from the 2012 Structural Specification §11.2. Original byte IRI identity and orientation; all ordered chains; top-property exemption, exact two-role transitivity, endpoint recursion, global transitivity and the literal inverse-source condition; inverse-source closure applies to direct targets, without assumed inverse-target invariance. The full finite worklist terminates without fuel. Raw node completeness excludes missing outcomes. Successful concrete relation is a strict order compatible with reverse hierarchy reachability; a rejected forced pair is contained in every permitted ordering. Canonical import assembly and all other DL restrictions remain separate.

requirements.requirement: DatatypeDefinitionAcyclicity
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual supplied complete raw axiom closure and exact IRI byte identity. The proved range collector derives every typed datatype dependency from all six range forms, including literal datatypes in enumerations/facet values; enclosing axiom annotations and untyped facet IRIs add no dependency. Directed reflexive reachability restores its owned input and is total even on repeated/cyclic finite graphs. Incremental checking accepts iff a strict partial order exists on the actual datatype carrier and includes every required smaller-to-defined pair. A rejected original dependency has a reverse path and proves no such order can exist. Nonempty transitive reachability constructs the mathematical order witness. No heuristic fuel or caller node metadata is assumed; this correctness-first graph search may take exponential time. Definition availability/uniqueness is separately proved and composed below; custom datatype literal/restriction positions, normative lexical/facet/value spaces, canonical imports, physical resources and complete DL validation remain separate obligations.

requirements.requirement: BuiltinVocabularyRestrictions
AxiomClosureValidation
ArityAndCardinalityValidation
requirements.implementation_scope: Complete standard unary raw OWL language: all 18 class forms, six data ranges and 37 annotated axiom variants. Unordered minimum-two associations count recursive structural equivalence classes, including cardinality omission defaults; required nonempty associations, ordered chain minimum written arity, unary data quantifiers and natural numbers follow from raw types. The explicitly accepted 2014 duplicate-disjointness compatibility rule requires pairwise different original members for DisjointClasses, DisjointUnion member classes, disjoint object/data properties and DifferentIndividuals; this is not an amendment to the 2012 Recommendation. Ordinary association repetitions are retained when two distinct members remain; ordered property chains may repeat. The full recursive closure operation composes these rules with the proved nonempty-key check, is total, accepts iff the independent conjunction holds and preserves the first original annotated failure. Input bytes, lexical/facet/value validity, canonical output, RDF self-disjointness mapping, import scoping and complete DL/reasoning validation remain separate.

requirements.implementation_scope: Numeric part only: facet_applies decides whether a range facet with a bound is in the facet space of owl:real, owl:rational, xsd:decimal, xsd:integer or an integer subtype exactly as OWL 2 §4.1 says (facet_applies_correct), and the ontology queries answer datatype restrictions of these datatypes by the four range facets with numeric bounds. requirements.requirement: ExactLexicalInterpretation
requirements.implementation_scope: Done for nineteen datatypes: literal_value returns a canonical value exactly for a lexical form in the lexical space of owl:rational, xsd:decimal, xsd:integer and its twelve subtypes, xsd:string, rdf:PlainLiteral and xsd:boolean (owl:real has none), and that value is the literal's value under every normative datatype map (literal_value_correct). requirements.requirement: ValueEquality
requirements.implementation_scope: Done for the nineteen datatypes of literal_value: canonical kernel values are equal exactly when their values are equal under every normative map (value_injective, same_value_correct), across datatypes too, so "1/4"^^owl:rational and "0.25"^^xsd:decimal are one value in the ontology queries. requirements.requirement: CrossDatatypeOverlap
requirements.implementation_scope: Done for the numeric datatypes, xsd:string, rdf:PlainLiteral and xsd:boolean: the ontology queries decide the overlaps of their value spaces (the integers inside the decimals inside the rationals inside the reals, the integer subtypes by their bounds as cuts of the reals, the strings inside the plain literals) and the disjointness of the numbers, the plain literals and the truth values. requirements.requirement: FiniteCardinality
requirements.implementation_scope: Done for the finite ranges of the supported datatypes: a bounded run of integers (an integer subtype such as xsd:byte, or a restriction between two bounds) has exactly its number of values, which the queries count exactly (an element can have 256 byte values but not 300), points of a single number have one value, and xsd:boolean has its two values. Finite ranges of the other datatypes are pending.

requirements.requirement: AtLeastN
requirements.implementation_scope: Done for the supported data ranges: an element can have at least n values of a range exactly when the range has n values, from infinite regions of numbers, strings and tagged strings or from a bounded run of integers, counted against a capacity that bounds the counts of the data restrictions of the closure and its questions. Ranges of the other datatypes are pending.

requirements.requirement: ConstraintSatisfiability
requirements.implementation_scope: Done for intersections, unions, complements and enumerations of the supported data ranges, with the four range facets on the numeric datatypes: the region encoding decides whether a combination of these constraints has a value (or n values). Constraints of the other datatypes and facets are pending.

requirements.requirement: DomainComplement
requirements.implementation_scope: Done for the supported data ranges: a complement holds of every value of the data domain outside the range, including the irrational reals outside owl:rational, the rationals outside xsd:decimal and values outside every supported datatype. Complements involving the other datatypes are pending.

requirements.requirement: Verified Functional Syntax lexical component: prefix_grammar_total_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: The four complete OWL Functional Syntax name languages (PNAME_NS, PN_LOCAL, PNAME_LN and BLANK_NODE_LABEL) use the referenced SPARQL 2008 character grammar. The actual compiled grammars equal independent Unicode-codepoint languages; whole-byte recognition terminates, accepts exactly each language and preserves exact malformed UTF-8 diagnostics even after grammar mismatch. requirements.requirement: Prefixed names scanned over ASCII bytes: ascii_prefix_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: Prefixed names scanned over ASCII bytes: names::ascii_prefix and names::ascii_abbreviated find the greatest PNAME_NS and PNAME_LN endpoint at a position without the grammars, by reading the run of ASCII label bytes (letters, digits, _, - and .), the colon right after it and, for PNAME_LN, the run after the colon up to its last byte other than a dot; they decline when a byte outside ASCII ends a run. Whenever they answer, the answer is proved to be the greatest candidate endpoint, or no endpoint, of the independent SPARQL 2008 languages (ascii_prefix_correct, ascii_abbreviated_correct). functional::longest_valid asks them before the grammar matcher, and longest_valid_eq keeps its statement, so the lexer's correctness theorems are unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Whole names recognized over ASCII bytes: whole_total_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: Whole names over ASCII bytes: names::validate_prefix, validate_local and validate_abbreviated, and functional::recognize for the two prefixed-name terminals, accept a buffer that the ASCII scan from its start reads whole (names::whole) without matching the grammar, and match the grammar otherwise. A span from the start that ends at the end of the bytes decodes all of them, so such a buffer is a well-encoded word of the language (whole_scan_accepted); the total-correctness and acceptance theorems of the validators and of recognize keep their statements.

requirements.requirement: Functional Syntax complete terminal disjointness: keyword_words_injective

requirements.requirement: Prefixed names scanned over ASCII bytes: ascii_name_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: Prefixed names scanned over ASCII bytes: names::ascii_prefix and names::ascii_abbreviated find the greatest PNAME_NS and PNAME_LN endpoint at a position without the grammars, by reading the run of ASCII label bytes (letters, digits, _, - and .), the colon right after it and, for PNAME_LN, the run after the colon up to its last byte other than a dot; they decline when a byte outside ASCII ends a run. Whenever they answer, the answer is proved to be the greatest candidate endpoint, or no endpoint, of the independent SPARQL 2008 languages (ascii_prefix_correct, ascii_abbreviated_correct). functional::longest_valid asks them before the grammar matcher, and longest_valid_eq keeps its statement, so the lexer's correctness theorems are unchanged.

requirements.implementation_scope: Functional Syntax source ontology identity and maximal leading import references after the proved original Ontology opening. The actual optional readers consume zero/one/two full or abbreviated IRI tokens and resolve their original spans; the SourceOntologyIdentity type permits a version only with an ontology IRI. Every import body checks all three syntax tokens before target IRI resolution; every Import keyword checks its count limit before body syntax. Repeated scanning terminates by exact three-body-token plus keyword progress, preserves original reference order, repetitions, keyword/IRI tokens and the untouched empty or first non-Import suffix. Total correctness and exact values/suffixes/first errors in both directions are proved for terminal discrimination, optional/identity reading, import skeleton/target construction, repeated scanning and the public low-level header-tail entry point. Header IRI values are exact source-linked final-budget-checked absolute IRIs. EOF syntax errors use the whole original source length; wrong terminals and IRI errors retain their established original offsets. Independent grammar/run relations also prove exact source values, bounded import count and maximal stopping. Source composition starts with actual complete byte prefix lexing/parsing and successful normative table checking, then proves exact header results/errors on precisely those source-derived namespace rows. The low-level reader itself receives tokens and a checked table, not a complete ontology document; unexpected trailing tokens are left unchanged for the full parser, and missing ontology body/closing syntax can still be accepted by this partial stage. Ontology annotations/axioms, complete document grammar/AST, canonical import catalog/closure assembly and anonymous scopes/provenance remain pending. Existing catalog closure still receives symbol/dependency metadata; these new source import IRI references are not yet a complete canonical import pipeline. All other original format, M3/M4 integration, normative datatype, SROIQ/query, physical resource/cancellation and full byte-to-answer release requirements remain unchanged and pending. Distinct frontend SourceOntologyIdentity naming avoids a pinned-extractor derived-instance collision with the kernel; generated code is not manually rewritten and no extraction assumption is added.

Members of intersections and unions are joined left-nested in source order. For either polarity, the result means exactly the expression or its complement under the independent Direct Semantics in every interpretation that fixes owl:Thing and owl:Nothing, which every OWL interpretation does, for object and data domains of any universe; concept instances therefore coincide with class instances. This is the first reasoner stage: the tableau, TBox reasoning, blocking, the remaining constructors, datatypes and query reductions remain pending. requirements.requirement: Verified ALC concept satisfiability without a TBox: toList_fromList
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual ALC concept-satisfiability procedure in the kernel, without a TBox: it decides whether some interpretation has an element in a negation-normal-form concept. Conjunctions are expanded, disjunctions branch, top is dropped and bottom rejects; once only named-class literals and restrictions remain, a named class occurring both positively and negated is a clash, and every existential restriction is decided recursively together with the universal restrictions on the same property, with properties and classes compared by exact IRI spelling. The procedure is proved total by well-founded recursion on the lexicographic pair of the total and the pending concept size. It is proved sound: every acceptance yields an explicit tree interpretation over paths whose root satisfies the concept, built from the successor models of the existential restrictions. It is proved complete: any interpretation in any universe with an element in the concept forces acceptance. Composed with the proved negation-normal-form translation, the tableau never rejects an OWL class expression with an instance in an OWL interpretation, so every rejection proves the expression empty in every OWL interpretation, which justifies unsatisfiability and subsumption answers for the ALC fragment. This is an internal fragment experiment toward M6: TBox axioms and blocking, the remaining SROIQ constructors, datatypes, the OWL-level tree model fixing owl:Thing and owl:Nothing, ontology-level query reductions and performance remain pending. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

Conjunctions are expanded, disjunctions branch, top is dropped and bottom rejects; once only named-class literals and restrictions remain, a named class occurring both positively and negated is a clash, and every existential restriction is decided recursively together with the universal restrictions on the same property, with properties and classes compared by exact IRI spelling. The procedure is proved total by well-founded recursion on the lexicographic pair of the total and the pending concept size. It is proved sound: every acceptance yields an explicit tree interpretation over paths whose root satisfies the concept, built from the successor models of the existential restrictions. It is proved complete: any interpretation in any universe with an element in the concept forces acceptance. Composed with the proved negation-normal-form translation, the tableau never rejects an OWL class expression with an instance in an OWL interpretation, so every rejection proves the expression empty in every OWL interpretation, which justifies unsatisfiability and subsumption answers for the ALC fragment. This is an internal fragment experiment toward M6: TBox axioms and blocking, the remaining SROIQ constructors, datatypes, the OWL-level tree model fixing owl:Thing and owl:Nothing, ontology-level query reductions and performance remain pending. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Verified SH concept satisfiability with respect to a TBox and role axioms, with blocking: sat_mono
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual SH concept-satisfiability procedure with respect to a TBox and role axioms in the kernel: tbox::satisfiable_with decides whether some interpretation in which a negation-normal-form TBox concept holds at every element and the object properties respect a role box (inclusions between named object properties, closed under composition, and transitive named object properties) has an element in a negation-normal-form concept; satisfiable_items does the same for a list of items. It runs the tableau with subset blocking on item lists, where a Through item stands for the universal restriction of a transitive property on a filler of the input. A successor along a property s receives the filler of every universal restriction on a property r with s below r and, for every transitive t with s below t and t below r, the restriction of t on that filler; inclusion is tested by the proved role_box::below. It is proved total by well-founded recursion on the remaining room 2^|closure| - |ancestors|, the total item size and the pending item size, where the finite closure adds to the subconcepts the universal restriction of every transitive property on every universal filler. It is proved sound through Hintikka families whose existential witnesses satisfy everything the universal restrictions require along the role (roleFillers): the interpretation whose elements are the sets of the family, relating two sets along a property when the second satisfies everything the first requires along it, is a model of the TBox concept with an instance of the input, and, when the listed inclusions include their compositions, it respects every listed inclusion and transitivity. It is proved complete: any interpretation in any universe that respects the role box, satisfies the TBox concept everywhere and has an instance of the input forces acceptance. The ALC entry points satisfiable_in and satisfiable_all run the same procedure with no role axioms and keep their proved ALC statements. The ontology queries read their role box from role axioms (alc_ontology::role_box); inverse roles, number restrictions, nominals, property chains, datatypes and performance remain pending. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

A successor along a property s receives the filler of every universal restriction on a property r with s below r and, for every transitive t with s below t and t below r, the restriction of t on that filler; inclusion is tested by the proved role_box::below. It is proved total by well-founded recursion on the remaining room 2^|closure| - |ancestors|, the total item size and the pending item size, where the finite closure adds to the subconcepts the universal restriction of every transitive property on every universal filler. It is proved sound through Hintikka families whose existential witnesses satisfy everything the universal restrictions require along the role (roleFillers): the interpretation whose elements are the sets of the family, relating two sets along a property when the second satisfies everything the first requires along it, is a model of the TBox concept with an instance of the input, and, when the listed inclusions include their compositions, it respects every listed inclusion and transitivity. It is proved complete: any interpretation in any universe that respects the role box, satisfies the TBox concept everywhere and has an instance of the input forces acceptance. The ALC entry points satisfiable_in and satisfiable_all run the same procedure with no role axioms and keep their proved ALC statements. The ontology queries read their role box from role axioms (alc_ontology::role_box); inverse roles, number restrictions, nominals, property chains, datatypes and performance remain pending. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Verified ALC concept satisfiability with respect to a TBox, with blocking: satisfiable_in_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual ALC concept-satisfiability procedure with respect to a TBox in the kernel: it decides whether some interpretation in which a negation-normal-form TBox concept holds at every element has an element in a negation-normal-form concept (general concept inclusions C ⊑ D can be supplied as the negation normal form of the conjunction of the unions of the complement of C with D). It runs the rules of the plain tableau, adds the TBox concept at the root and at every successor, and blocks, and accepts, a node whose literal set is contained in the literal set of an ancestor on its branch; concepts are compared structurally by exact IRI spelling. It is proved total by well-founded recursion on the lexicographic triple of the remaining room 2^|closure| - |ancestors|, the total concept size and the pending concept size: every unblocked node adds a literal set from the finite subconcept closure of the input and TBox concepts that differs from all of its ancestors' sets, which bounds every branch. It is proved sound through a Hintikka-family certificate: every acceptance yields a finite family of clash-free literal sets that each satisfy the TBox concept, with every existential restriction witnessed inside the family together with the universal restrictions on its property, and the interpretation whose elements are those sets is a model of the TBox concept with an instance of the input concept. It is proved complete: any interpretation in any universe in which the TBox concept holds everywhere and the input concept has an instance forces acceptance. Composed with the proved negation-normal-form translation, the procedure never rejects an OWL class expression with an instance in an OWL interpretation in which the TBox class expression holds at every element, so every rejection proves the expression empty in all such interpretations. This is an internal fragment experiment toward M6; the ontology-level queries and role axioms built on it are separate entries, and the remaining SROIQ constructors, datatypes and performance remain pending. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Verified ontology-level ALC consistency, class satisfiability, subsumption and instance checking: all_equal_iff
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual ontology-level reasoning in the kernel for ALC with assertions about individuals and role axioms (SH): consistency, class satisfiability, subsumption and instance checking with respect to an axiom closure. Every supported class axiom is internalized into a negation-normal-form concept that holds at every element exactly when the axiom holds: SubClassOf(C D) becomes the union of the complement of C with D, EquivalentClasses holds all members together or none, DisjointClasses excludes every two member occurrences, DisjointUnion also equates the class with the union of its members, ObjectPropertyDomain and ObjectPropertyRange on a named object property restrict its sources or targets, and declarations, annotation axioms, assertions and role axioms impose nothing; the closure's TBox concept is their conjunction, proved to hold at every element exactly when an interpretation fixing owl:Thing and owl:Nothing satisfies every axiom that is neither an assertion nor a role axiom. SubObjectPropertyOf with a single named sub-property and a named super-property, EquivalentObjectProperties of named properties and TransitiveObjectProperty of a named property form a role box whose inclusions are closed under composition (each new inclusion adds every inclusion it composes with), proved to be respected by an interpretation exactly when it satisfies these role axioms. Every individual that an assertion mentions gets a node, interned by exact structural equality, and node 0 stands for one further element. ClassAssertion becomes the translated concept at its individual's node, ObjectPropertyAssertion an edge along its named property (an inverse property reverses it), and a NegativeObjectPropertyAssertion contradicts the closure exactly when the same edge is asserted; together with role axioms a negative assertion has no answer yet. The queries add their concepts at node 0 or at the queried individual's node and decide with the verified completion for named individuals under that role box. They answer exactly when the internalization, the role box and all translations succeed, no translated concept uses a built-in object property as a role or a built-in class as an ordinary named class, no assertion or role axiom uses a built-in object property, no negative property assertion occurs together with role axioms, and there is room for the nodes, placed concepts and role box. Each answer is proved to equal the independent Direct Semantics definitions of Consistent, ClassSatisfiable, Subsumed and InstanceOf for any valid vocabulary: every acceptance is turned into an actual OWL model of the closure, built from the completion's model with every individual at its node and every other object property read as there, so that the role axioms hold, the built-in classes and object and data properties fixed and data values, datatypes, literals and facets taken from the datatype map, and every OWL model, in any universe and with any reinterpretation of its anonymous individuals, forces acceptance. SameIndividual, DifferentIndividuals, data assertions, negative property assertions together with role axioms, inverse properties and property chains in role axioms, disjoint and inverse property axioms, the other property characteristics, the other axiom forms, the remaining SROIQ constructors, datatypes, query answering and performance remain pending. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

It reads exactly one such axiom at a caller-supplied position: the keyword, the opening parenthesis, the axiom annotations with the proved annotation reader and its limits, the body, then the closing parenthesis. Bodies use the proved class-expression and object-property readers at the full nesting allowance. Equivalent, disjoint and disjoint-union member lists are the maximal member sequence followed by the two-member minimum, and the disjoint union's class IRI resolves through the checked prefix table. Errors return the first failing step in source order with original offsets; EOF errors use the source length. Original keyword and IRI tokens and the unchanged suffix are retained. Original-byte prefix parsing and normative checked-table construction compose with the reader using precisely those source namespace rows; the caller still supplies the axiom position. The other axiom forms remain pending; the axiom loop, the closing token and the mapping into the kernel's ontology model are proved as the document and model stages. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Axiom family total correct for exact whole-document source reading
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual whole-document Functional Syntax reading is total and has exact result/error equivalence. From the original bytes it reads the prefix declarations with the proved prefix-header reader and checks them with the normative table checker, then reads everything after Ontology( with an independent grammar: the ontology identity and imports, the maximal ontology-annotation sequence, the axiom loop, the closing parenthesis, and the end of the source. The axiom loop dispatches on all 37 axiom keywords: declarations, the four annotation axioms, SubClassOf, EquivalentClasses, DisjointClasses, DisjointUnion, ObjectPropertyDomain and ObjectPropertyRange, the eleven object property axioms, the eight data property axioms, datatype definitions and keys, and the seven assertions go to their proved readers with the caller's limits, so every axiom form is read. An axiom count limit bounds the loop; it is checked before each axiom is read. Errors report the first failing stage in source order with original offsets: a prefix-header failure, a rejected namespace table by kind, a header or annotation failure, an axiom-level failure with its stage, a token that cannot start an axiom, the end of the source before the closing parenthesis, or content after it. The loop is proved total by well-founded recursion on the token count, using the proved minimum token consumption of every axiom reader; every derivation is the actual result, and an accepted document keeps the original prefix declarations and the exact source records in order. Canonical imports and anonymous-individual scopes across documents remain pending; the mapping of the records into the kernel's raw OWL model is proved as the model stage. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Copy bytes correct for the raw OWL model of read documents
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual mapping of a read Functional Syntax document into the kernel's raw OWL model, proved total and exact against an independent structural correspondence. Every IRI and literal keeps its exact bytes (a plain literal keeps its reader-normalized lexical form and datatype), node IDs become anonymous individuals of a caller-supplied scope, original tokens are dropped, and nested annotations, class expressions, member lists, individual lists, imports, ontology annotations and axioms keep their source order: declarations become entity declarations, the four annotation axioms keep their subjects and values, the six class axioms keep their class expressions, including object properties and their inverses, the named or anonymous individuals of enumerations and value restrictions, self restrictions, number restrictions with their numbers as unary naturals and their optional fillers, and data restrictions with their data properties, literals and data ranges (datatypes, intersections, unions, complements, literal enumerations and datatype restrictions with their facets, in source order), SameIndividual and DifferentIndividuals keep their individual lists, class and positive and negative object and data property assertions keep their class expression or property, their named or anonymous individuals and their literals, and data property axioms, datatype definitions and keys keep their data properties, class expressions, data ranges and property lists in source order. The mapping declines only a member list or individual list with fewer than two members or an enumeration or datatype restriction without members; independent grammar invariants prove that every class expression, class axiom, assertion and axiom the document grammar accepts has at least two members in each such list and one in each enumeration, so every document the reader accepts maps. Canonical imports and anonymous-individual scopes assigned across an import closure remain pending. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Verified reasoning with named individuals under role axioms (SH): nodeFillers_mem
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual reasoning with named individuals under role axioms (SH) in the kernel: abox_satisfiable_with decides whether some interpretation in which a negation-normal-form TBox concept holds at every element and the object properties respect a role box (inclusions between named object properties, closed under composition, and transitive named object properties) has an element for every node below a positive count that satisfies the given facts (concepts at nodes, or Through facts standing for universal restrictions on transitive properties) and edges (named object properties between nodes). The completion adds the TBox concept at every node, then adds each fact once: it expands conjunctions, branches on disjunctions and pushes every universal restriction along each edge whose property it includes, giving the target the filler and the restriction on every transitive property in between. Once no fact is pending it checks every node for a clash and decides every existential restriction with the SH TBox tableau, together with what the universal restrictions at the same node require along its role. Termination is proved from the measure (node-closure pairs not yet added, pending facts) over a closure extended with the transitive restrictions. Every acceptance under a closed role box yields an explicit model of the role axioms: one element per node and a disjoint copy of a successor model for every existential obligation, related by single steps along included properties and by paths along transitive ones; it relates node elements exactly as the edges and role axioms entail (an edge along an included property, or a path of such edges along a transitive property). Every model of the role axioms in any universe forces acceptance. The ALC entry point abox_satisfiable is the procedure without role axioms and keeps its proved statement. The ontology queries run it with the role box read from their role axioms; equality between individuals, inverse roles, number restrictions and nominals remain pending. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Verified role boxes from the role axioms of an ontology: copy_property_identity
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual ontology-level reasoning in the kernel for ALC with assertions about individuals and role axioms (SH): consistency, class satisfiability, subsumption and instance checking with respect to an axiom closure. Every supported class axiom is internalized into a negation-normal-form concept that holds at every element exactly when the axiom holds: SubClassOf(C D) becomes the union of the complement of C with D, EquivalentClasses holds all members together or none, DisjointClasses excludes every two member occurrences, DisjointUnion also equates the class with the union of its members, ObjectPropertyDomain and ObjectPropertyRange on a named object property restrict its sources or targets, and declarations, annotation axioms, assertions and role axioms impose nothing; the closure's TBox concept is their conjunction, proved to hold at every element exactly when an interpretation fixing owl:Thing and owl:Nothing satisfies every axiom that is neither an assertion nor a role axiom. SubObjectPropertyOf with a single named sub-property and a named super-property, EquivalentObjectProperties of named properties and TransitiveObjectProperty of a named property form a role box whose inclusions are closed under composition (each new inclusion adds every inclusion it composes with), proved to be respected by an interpretation exactly when it satisfies these role axioms. Every individual that an assertion mentions gets a node, interned by exact structural equality, and node 0 stands for one further element. ClassAssertion becomes the translated concept at its individual's node, ObjectPropertyAssertion an edge along its named property (an inverse property reverses it), and a NegativeObjectPropertyAssertion contradicts the closure exactly when the same edge is asserted; together with role axioms a negative assertion has no answer yet. The queries add their concepts at node 0 or at the queried individual's node and decide with the verified completion for named individuals under that role box. They answer exactly when the internalization, the role box and all translations succeed, no translated concept uses a built-in object property as a role or a built-in class as an ordinary named class, no assertion or role axiom uses a built-in object property, no negative property assertion occurs together with role axioms, and there is room for the nodes, placed concepts and role box. Each answer is proved to equal the independent Direct Semantics definitions of Consistent, ClassSatisfiable, Subsumed and InstanceOf for any valid vocabulary: every acceptance is turned into an actual OWL model of the closure, built from the completion's model with every individual at its node and every other object property read as there, so that the role axioms hold, the built-in classes and object and data properties fixed and data values, datatypes, literals and facets taken from the datatype map, and every OWL model, in any universe and with any reinterpretation of its anonymous individuals, forces acceptance. SameIndividual, DifferentIndividuals, data assertions, negative property assertions together with role axioms, inverse properties and property chains in role axioms, disjoint and inverse property axioms, the other property characteristics, the other axiom forms, the remaining SROIQ constructors, datatypes, query answering and performance remain pending. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Verified rule search of the completion graph tableau: contains_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual rule search of the completion graph tableau for SHI with named individuals, proved exact against independent predicates on its lists. A label is a list of indices of literal entries of the concept table; Holds reads conjunctions and disjunctions propositionally and every other entry as membership, and holds is proved to decide it. The searches are proved to return, in a fixed order, a node and an entry it needs and lacks (a requirement at the node, the TBox concept, the concept of a lazy unfolding A ⊑ C whose class the label lists, or what a universal restriction at the other end of a link or tree edge requires along the edge's role in either direction, including the restriction on every transitive role in between), else an unblocked node with an existential restriction without a witness (a child created along an included role, the parent along the inverse of the creating role, or a linked named node, satisfying the filler), else Done exactly when no rule applies (Complete). Blocking is anywhere equality blocking: a tree node is blocked when its parent is, or when an earlier tree node that is not blocked has a label of the same length with the same items (Blocked); blocking computes the flags of all nodes in one pass in index order and is proved to decide it for every node (blocks_correct, repeated_before_correct, blocked_at_correct, blocking_correct). Clashes between a named class, a nominal or a self restriction and its complement are detected by an exact search. The tableau's termination, soundness and completeness are proved separately (Rowl.Completion). No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Verified completion graph tableau: copy_label_correct

Clashes are detected on insertion; definitions A ⊑ C are unfolded lazily. satisfiable interns the facts, the TBox concept and the definitions, closes the table under the restrictions of transitive roles and runs the tableau from one blank named node per individual. An acceptance is proved to come with a model (in Type) of the role hierarchy in which the TBox concept and every definition hold everywhere and every fact and link holds at its named nodes, with named nodes related only along links when there are no role axioms and different named nodes as different elements; a rejection is proved to rule out every such model in any universes. Every node records the branch points its label depends on: a rule adds to a node with the points of the node and its neighbours (rule_deps), a new tree node starts with its parent's points, and a clash reports the points of its node and of the clashing entry. Disjunctions branch on copies of the graph under a fresh branch point; when the left disjunct fails with a clash set without that point, the right disjunct is skipped, otherwise it is tried with the points the failure depended on. A rejection with clash set D is proved to rule out every model, in any universes, that satisfies the label of every node whose points lie in D (FullModel). Clashes are detected on insertion; definitions A ⊑ C are unfolded lazily. satisfiable interns the facts, the TBox concept and the definitions, closes the table under the restrictions of transitive roles and runs the tableau from one blank named node per individual. An acceptance is proved to come with a model (in Type) of the role hierarchy in which the TBox concept and every definition hold everywhere and every fact and link holds at its named nodes, with named nodes related only along links when there are no role axioms and different named nodes as different elements; a rejection is proved to rule out every such model in any universes. A nominal, a self restriction or a cardinality restriction that reaches a label gives no answer, and otherwise None reports only a usize capacity limit.

Every node records the branch points its label depends on: a rule adds to a node with the points of the node and its neighbours (rule_deps), a new tree node starts with its parent's points, and a clash reports the points of its node and of the clashing entry. Disjunctions branch on copies of the graph under a fresh branch point; when the left disjunct fails with a clash set without that point, the right disjunct is skipped, otherwise it is tried with the points the failure depended on. A rejection with clash set D is proved to rule out every model, in any universes, that satisfies the label of every node whose points lie in D (FullModel). Clashes are detected on insertion; definitions A ⊑ C are unfolded lazily. satisfiable interns the facts, the TBox concept and the definitions, closes the table under the restrictions of transitive roles and runs the tableau from one blank named node per individual. An acceptance is proved to come with a model (in Type) of the role hierarchy in which the TBox concept and every definition hold everywhere and every fact and link holds at its named nodes, with named nodes related only along links when there are no role axioms and different named nodes as different elements; a rejection is proved to rule out every such model in any universes. A nominal, a self restriction or a cardinality restriction that reaches a label gives no answer, and otherwise None reports only a usize capacity limit.

requirements.requirement: Verified completion graph tableau: copy_entries_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: A base prepared once for many queries: completion::base interns the facts, the TBox concept and the definitions and closes the table once, and is proved to give a well-formed table whose TBox index, requirements and unfoldings mean exactly those inputs (BaseFor). completion::satisfiable_from interns a query into an exact copy of the base's table, closes it again and runs the tableau; it is proved to give exactly the guarantees of satisfiable on the base's facts, TBox concept and definitions, so an accepting answer yields a model and a rejection excludes every model in any universes. The prepared SHI queries of shi_ontology use the base whenever it fits.

requirements.requirement: Verified class parts with absorption: copy_iri_class
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual class parts of an axiom closure for the tableaux (shi_ontology::class_parts), proved against the Direct Semantics. Every class axiom over translatable class expressions becomes inclusions: a subclass axiom one, equivalent classes the first member in every other member and back, disjoint classes every member in the complement of every later member, and a disjoint union the class in the union of its members and every member in the class, which the members also partition. An inclusion with an absorbable left side becomes a definition A ⊑ C unfolded lazily (a named class directly, ∃r.E ⊑ D as E ⊑ ∀r⁻.D, and E ⊓ F ⊓ … ⊑ D as E ⊑ ¬F ⊔ … ⊔ D); every other inclusion conjoins ¬C ⊔ D onto the TBox concept, a domain or range of an object property expression conjoins ∀r⁻.C or ∀r.C, a functional or inverse functional object property conjoins ≤1 r.⊤ or ≤1 r⁻.⊤, and a reflexive or irreflexive object property conjoins ∃r.Self or ¬∃r.Self. Assertions, individual equalities and inequalities, role axioms, asymmetric and disjoint object properties (ConstraintAxiom) and property chains (ChainAxiom) add no part. In every interpretation fixing owl:Thing and owl:Nothing the TBox concept holds everywhere and the definitions hold exactly when every class axiom holds; the parts are computed only for supported axioms, and always when every axiom is supported and the definitions fit in the usize range.

requirements.requirement: Verified SHI ontology queries on the completion graph tableau: proper_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual consistency, class satisfiability, subsumption and instance checking for SROIQ axiom closures, with the universal and empty roles, self restrictions, asymmetric and disjoint object properties, property chains and assertions and individual equalities and inequalities (shi_ontology), decided by the verified completion graph tableau or by the verified completion forest, and proved exact for the OWL 2 Direct Semantics in any universes. Class axioms over ALCIQO expressions become the TBox concept and lazily unfolded definitions, functional and inverse functional object properties maximum restrictions and reflexive and irreflexive object properties self restrictions and their complements in the TBox concept, the role axioms (inclusions without chains, equivalences, inverses, symmetry and transitivity of object property expressions) a closed role hierarchy, asymmetric and disjoint object properties its disjoint pairs, property chains its role chains (Rowl.Chains), owl:bottomObjectProperty an ordinary role whose emptiness the TBox concept also requires as ∀B.⊥ (withEmpty, shi_ontology::empty_role), so that it relates nothing in the tableaux's models, as OWL requires, class assertions and query concepts facts at the nodes of their individuals, and object property assertions links; the members of every SameIndividual axiom share the node of their representative, and the individuals of the nominals of the closure get nodes too. A question whose concepts have no number restriction, self restriction or nominal, about a closure without negative assertions next to role axioms, without disjoint pairs (shi_ontology::constrained) and without role chains (shi_ontology::chained), goes to the completion graph tableau, whose models keep different nodes apart: there a negative object property assertion is refuted exactly by a link in either orientation between its individuals' nodes, and a DifferentIndividuals axiom exactly when two of its members share a node. Every other question goes to the completion forest, with the role chains encoded in front of it (role_chains::satisfiable), which merges individuals when a maximum restriction or a nominal requires it, with the nominal of every individual at its node, the members of every inequality outside the nominals of the later members, and the universal restriction to the complement of the target's nominal at the source of every negative assertion as further facts (Rowl.ShiNominals). An acceptance comes with an actual OWL model of the closure built from the tableau's model, with every individual at its node, which is where the forest's model places the individual of every nominal, and every OWL model forces acceptance. The queries answer only on supported axioms and Translatable expressions whose nominals are of named individuals, in a question only of individuals the closure has; a question whose closure or concepts use owl:topObjectProperty goes to the completion forest over the guesses for the restrictions along it (Rowl.Universal, universal::satisfiable, shi_ontology::closure_universal), and its acceptances come with an OWL model built from the forest's model once the universal role relates every pair (withUniversal), which keeps every role axiom of the closure (universal_role_axiom, universal_constraint_axiom, universal_chain_axiom); no answer is given for number restrictions along owl:topObjectProperty or role axioms that include it in another role or make it inverse, equivalent, asymmetric or disjoint (universal::not_top, RoleProper, shi_ontology::inclusion_proper), for number restrictions, complements of self restrictions and disjoint pairs on roles that are not simple, which includes every role that the role of a chain is included in, when the role chains are not regular, when a bound of the completion forest from new named nodes has fewer counted named neighbours than it allows or the table has no self restriction for an edge that a merge of the forest turns into loops, or when a usize limit is reached.

requirements.requirement: Verified universal role through a case split: not_top_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual decision of the universal role owl:topObjectProperty for the completion forest through a case split (universal::satisfiable, Rowl.Universal), proved against the Direct Semantics in any universes. A restriction along the universal role, ∃U.C or ∀U.C in either orientation (Global), holds at every element or at none once the universal role relates every pair (withUniversal, global_denote), so its truth is one global choice (GlobalTruth). The atoms are collected once each from the TBox concept, the definitions and the facts, with every atom that occurs in them (universal::collect, collect_correct, same_concept_correct, atom_index_correct); under a guess every atom becomes ⊤ or ⊥ and ∃U.Self ⊤ and its complement ⊥ (fixedOf, fixed_correct), and the guess is made good by what it requires (Required, require_correct): a further element at a further node in the filler of a true ∃U.C or outside the filler of a false ∀U.C, and the filler of a true ∀U.C or the complement of the filler of a false ∃U.C in the TBox concept. The completion forest with the role chains in front of it decides each guess (guessed_correct), and the search tries the guesses in turn (guesses_correct), at most 2^16 of them. In a model of a guess's requirements every guess is the truth of its atom, the atoms of a filler first (requirements_exact), so the concepts under the guess mean the concepts once the universal role relates every pair (fixed_meaning); a model of the question in which the universal role relates every pair is a model of the guess of its own truths, with its witnesses at the further nodes, so the search accepts (satisfiable_correct). Number restrictions must not count along the universal role (NoTopCount).

requirements.implementation_scope: Actual consistency, class satisfiability, subsumption and instance checking for SROIQ axiom closures, with the universal and empty roles, self restrictions, asymmetric and disjoint object properties, property chains and assertions and individual equalities and inequalities (shi_ontology), decided by the verified completion graph tableau or by the verified completion forest, and proved exact for the OWL 2 Direct Semantics in any universes. Class axioms over ALCIQO expressions become the TBox concept and lazily unfolded definitions, functional and inverse functional object properties maximum restrictions and reflexive and irreflexive object properties self restrictions and their complements in the TBox concept, the role axioms (inclusions without chains, equivalences, inverses, symmetry and transitivity of object property expressions) a closed role hierarchy, asymmetric and disjoint object properties its disjoint pairs, property chains its role chains (Rowl.Chains), owl:bottomObjectProperty an ordinary role whose emptiness the TBox concept also requires as ∀B.⊥ (withEmpty, shi_ontology::empty_role), so that it relates nothing in the tableaux's models, as OWL requires, class assertions and query concepts facts at the nodes of their individuals, and object property assertions links; the members of every SameIndividual axiom share the node of their representative, and the individuals of the nominals of the closure get nodes too. A question whose concepts have no number restriction, self restriction or nominal, about a closure without negative assertions next to role axioms, without disjoint pairs (shi_ontology::constrained) and without role chains (shi_ontology::chained), goes to the completion graph tableau, whose models keep different nodes apart: there a negative object property assertion is refuted exactly by a link in either orientation between its individuals' nodes, and a DifferentIndividuals axiom exactly when two of its members share a node. Every other question goes to the completion forest, with the role chains encoded in front of it (role_chains::satisfiable), which merges individuals when a maximum restriction or a nominal requires it, with the nominal of every individual at its node, the members of every inequality outside the nominals of the later members, and the universal restriction to the complement of the target's nominal at the source of every negative assertion as further facts (Rowl.ShiNominals). An acceptance comes with an actual OWL model of the closure built from the tableau's model, with every individual at its node, which is where the forest's model places the individual of every nominal, and every OWL model forces acceptance. The queries answer only on supported axioms and Translatable expressions whose nominals are of named individuals, in a question only of individuals the closure has; a question whose closure or concepts use owl:topObjectProperty goes to the completion forest over the guesses for the restrictions along it (Rowl.Universal, universal::satisfiable, shi_ontology::closure_universal), and its acceptances come with an OWL model built from the forest's model once the universal role relates every pair (withUniversal), which keeps every role axiom of the closure (universal_role_axiom, universal_constraint_axiom, universal_chain_axiom); no answer is given for number restrictions along owl:topObjectProperty or role axioms that include it in another role or make it inverse, equivalent, asymmetric or disjoint (universal::not_top, RoleProper, shi_ontology::inclusion_proper), for number restrictions, complements of self restrictions and disjoint pairs on roles that are not simple, which includes every role that the role of a chain is included in, when the role chains are not regular, when a bound of the completion forest from new named nodes has fewer counted named neighbours than it allows or the table has no self restriction for an edge that a merge of the forest turns into loops, or when a usize limit is reached.

requirements.requirement: Verified rule search of the completion forest: representative_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual rule search of the completion forest for SHOIQ with named individuals (forest::next_step). The forest has one root per named individual and trees of anonymous nodes; a tree node's edge from its parent carries a list of roles, merges of named nodes are read through the individuals' representatives (same), and merges of tree nodes into named nodes add edges from their parents, named or tree nodes, to named nodes. The neighbours of a node along a role (forest::neighbours) are proved to be listed exactly and once each: its active children along an included role, its parent along an included inverse role, the named nodes that a link relates to it, the nodes that an added edge from a live node (active and not blocked: Live, forest::live) relates to it, and the node itself when a self restriction ∃s.Self of its label is a loop along a role whose inverse or itself is included (SelfAlong, forest::looping, forest::self_along, forest::loops_along). The named node of an individual (NominalRoot, forest::nominal_root) is the representative of the node of the first requirement with its nominal. The search is proved exact: it returns a concept that an active node lacks and that the requirements of the individuals merged into it, the TBox concept, an unfolding or its seed requires, a tree node or a named node beyond the individuals' nodes having a seed (Seeded, forest::seeded), or that a tree edge, a link, an added edge from a live node or a loop requires of either end (AddNeeds, LoopNeeds, forest::missing_loop, forest::missing_loops); requirements.requirement: Verified operation of the completion forest: copy_roles_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual operations the rules of the completion forest apply (forest.rs), each proved exact: copying the forest reproduces it, with its bounds from new named nodes (forest::copy_caps); adding an item to a label appends it and joins the branch points; the pending entries of a label list it; creating children appends that many tree nodes with one role, the seed and the given points; differences between new nodes cover exactly the pairs among them; new named nodes for a maximum restriction (forest::fresh_named, forest::named, freshNode, NamedMade) come after the old nodes with the filler as their seed and an added edge from the node, pairwise different, with the bound on the neighbours the restriction counts; the named nodes and the first tree node that is no child of a node in a list are found exactly (forest::named_of, forest::first_repeated); the branch points a rule rests on cover the nodes near it (its parent, active children and the named nodes a link or added edge relates to it) and the added edges at it, and come from nodes and edges only; the differences among chosen nodes, the pairs of chosen nodes not known to differ, the first nodes of a list, the orientation of a pair, which merges one of its nodes into the other (orient_either), are as specified, also for a tree node and its own tree child or parent, which only a loop makes neighbours, as the merge of the child into its parent; whether a node is the tree parent of a tree node (IntoParent, forest::into_parent) and the self restrictions for loops along a role or its inverse (forest::loop_for, forest::loop_entry, forest::loops_of) are found exactly; and the parts of a merge are exact: moving the roles of a merged child onto the parent edge or a sibling, adding edges from the parent of a merged tree node to a named node, carrying the added edges of a merged tree node over to the target (forest::carried, CarriedEdge), renaming an individual's representative, relinking the added edges at a merged named node to the target (forest::relink, forest::relinked, RelinkedEdge), inheriting the differences of the merged node, and pruning, which deactivates every tree node below an inactive parent.

requirements.requirement: Verified structural step of the completion forest: expanded_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: The structural steps of the completion forest (forest::expanded, forest::moved, forest::merged, forest::named), proved exact and proved to keep the invariant, to decrease the measure and to carry models over. Expanding an existential or minimum restriction of an active unblocked node appends its children along its role with its filler as their seed and the node's branch points, pairwise different, and marks the restriction as expanded; the node loses more weight than all its new children carry, and a model where the restriction holds at the node has different witnesses for the children (created_models). A merge of one node into another (MergeShape), of two neighbours of a node oriented as forest::orient does (orient_shape), or of a node into the named node of its nominal, hands the edge of a merged tree node over to its grandparent, to a sibling or, as an added edge from its parent, to a named node, or keeps the edges for a merge into its tree parent, whose loops the merge adds (moved_refl), and carries its added edges over to the target (moved_carried), or passes the individuals and the added edges of a merged named node on; inherits its differences; deactivates it with its subtree; and makes the target depend on the merge (Merged); the merged node no longer counts in the measure, and a model that places both nodes on one element models the merged forest with the label of the merged node at the target (merged_models). New named nodes for a maximum restriction of an active named node without a bound keep the invariant (named_inv) and decrease the measure, since the restriction loses more weight than they and their own restrictions bring (named_measure), and a model where the node has exactly as many counted neighbours as new nodes places them on those neighbours (named_models).

Expanding an existential or minimum restriction of an active unblocked node appends its children along its role with its filler as their seed and the node's branch points, pairwise different, and marks the restriction as expanded; the node loses more weight than all its new children carry, and a model where the restriction holds at the node has different witnesses for the children (created_models). A merge of one node into another (MergeShape), of two neighbours of a node oriented as forest::orient does (orient_shape), or of a node into the named node of its nominal, hands the edge of a merged tree node over to its grandparent, to a sibling or, as an added edge from its parent, to a named node, or keeps the edges for a merge into its tree parent, whose loops the merge adds (moved_refl), and carries its added edges over to the target (moved_carried), or passes the individuals and the added edges of a merged named node on; inherits its differences; deactivates it with its subtree; and makes the target depend on the merge (Merged); the merged node no longer counts in the measure, and a model that places both nodes on one element models the merged forest with the label of the merged node at the target (merged_models). New named nodes for a maximum restriction of an active named node without a bound keep the invariant (named_inv) and decrease the measure, since the restriction loses more weight than they and their own restrictions bring (named_measure), and a model where the node has exactly as many counted neighbours as new nodes places them on those neighbours (named_models).

A merge of one node into another (MergeShape), of two neighbours of a node oriented as forest::orient does (orient_shape), or of a node into the named node of its nominal, hands the edge of a merged tree node over to its grandparent, to a sibling or, as an added edge from its parent, to a named node, or keeps the edges for a merge into its tree parent, whose loops the merge adds (moved_refl), and carries its added edges over to the target (moved_carried), or passes the individuals and the added edges of a merged named node on; inherits its differences; deactivates it with its subtree; and makes the target depend on the merge (Merged); the merged node no longer counts in the measure, and a model that places both nodes on one element models the merged forest with the label of the merged node at the target (merged_models). New named nodes for a maximum restriction of an active named node without a bound keep the invariant (named_inv) and decrease the measure, since the restriction loses more weight than they and their own restrictions bring (named_measure), and a model where the node has exactly as many counted neighbours as new nodes places them on those neighbours (named_models).

requirements.requirement: Verified run of the completion forest: holds_literal
requirements.implementation_scope: Termination of the completion forest for SHOIQ and the meaning of its rejections (forest::run, forest::satisfiable). Every rule application adds a literal to the label of an active node, expands a restriction of an unblocked node, merges two neighbours, merges a node into the named node of its nominal, or creates new named nodes for a maximum restriction of a named node, and each decreases the measure, so run terminates on every forest that keeps the invariant (run_correct); a node with ¬∃r.Self that is its own neighbour along r, through a loop, a link or an added edge, is a clash, since every model relates it to itself along r, and so is a node with a common neighbour along both roles of a disjoint pair. An acceptance comes with a complete forest that keeps the invariant; a rejection with a set of branch points below the next free one rules out every model, in any universes, that holds under those points. Branching on a disjunction or on a neighbour's choice for a maximum restriction retries the second alternative only when the first failure depends on the new branch point (branch_correct); the merge rule tries the pairs of its first n + 1 counted neighbours that are not known to differ in turn, since in every model of the restriction two of them coincide (merge_rule_correct, choices_correct); a merge into the tree parent adds to the parent the self restrictions for loops along the roles of the merged edge, which every model where the two nodes coincide satisfies (merge_correct). Every model places a node with a nominal and the named node of its individual on the individual, so the merge of the nominal rule, at any depth, is forced and a difference between them is a clash (nominal_correct). Every model of a maximum restriction of a named node that counts a neighbour has an exact number of counted neighbours between 1 and its bound (exactly_between), so the rule for new named nodes tries the guesses in turn with backjumping (guesses_correct, named_rejected, name_rule_correct), and with the bound a guess records, the counted tree node that is no child of the node coincides with one of as many counted named neighbours in every model (capped_rule_correct). forest::satisfiable interns the facts, the TBox concept and the definitions and the self restriction of the role of every existential and minimum restriction (forest::loop_entries, loop_entries_correct), closes the table under the transitive roles, declines number restrictions, complements of self restrictions and disjoint pairs on roles that are not simple (CountsSimply, forest::disjoint_simple), starts from one root per individual and runs the forest; it is proved to terminate, its false answers rule out every model of the role hierarchy, the TBox concept, the definitions, the facts and the links, and its true answers come with a complete forest that keeps the invariant for the interned input (satisfiable_answers); it gives no answer when a structure would exceed the usize range, a number restriction, the complement of a self restriction or a disjoint pair is on a non-simple role, a restriction with a bound from new named nodes has fewer counted named neighbours than the bound, the individual of a nominal or of the complement of one has no named node, or the table has no self restriction for a role of an edge that a merge into a tree parent turns into loops. The model of a complete forest, and with it the exactness of true answers, is proved in Rowl.ForestModel.

Every rule application adds a literal to the label of an active node, expands a restriction of an unblocked node, merges two neighbours, merges a node into the named node of its nominal, or creates new named nodes for a maximum restriction of a named node, and each decreases the measure, so run terminates on every forest that keeps the invariant (run_correct); a node with ¬∃r.Self that is its own neighbour along r, through a loop, a link or an added edge, is a clash, since every model relates it to itself along r, and so is a node with a common neighbour along both roles of a disjoint pair. An acceptance comes with a complete forest that keeps the invariant; a rejection with a set of branch points below the next free one rules out every model, in any universes, that holds under those points. Branching on a disjunction or on a neighbour's choice for a maximum restriction retries the second alternative only when the first failure depends on the new branch point (branch_correct); the merge rule tries the pairs of its first n + 1 counted neighbours that are not known to differ in turn, since in every model of the restriction two of them coincide (merge_rule_correct, choices_correct); a merge into the tree parent adds to the parent the self restrictions for loops along the roles of the merged edge, which every model where the two nodes coincide satisfies (merge_correct). Every model places a node with a nominal and the named node of its individual on the individual, so the merge of the nominal rule, at any depth, is forced and a difference between them is a clash (nominal_correct). Every model of a maximum restriction of a named node that counts a neighbour has an exact number of counted neighbours between 1 and its bound (exactly_between), so the rule for new named nodes tries the guesses in turn with backjumping (guesses_correct, named_rejected, name_rule_correct), and with the bound a guess records, the counted tree node that is no child of the node coincides with one of as many counted named neighbours in every model (capped_rule_correct). forest::satisfiable interns the facts, the TBox concept and the definitions and the self restriction of the role of every existential and minimum restriction (forest::loop_entries, loop_entries_correct), closes the table under the transitive roles, declines number restrictions, complements of self restrictions and disjoint pairs on roles that are not simple (CountsSimply, forest::disjoint_simple), starts from one root per individual and runs the forest; it is proved to terminate, its false answers rule out every model of the role hierarchy, the TBox concept, the definitions, the facts and the links, and its true answers come with a complete forest that keeps the invariant for the interned input (satisfiable_answers); it gives no answer when a structure would exceed the usize range, a number restriction, the complement of a self restriction or a disjoint pair is on a non-simple role, a restriction with a bound from new named nodes has fewer counted named neighbours than the bound, the individual of a nominal or of the complement of one has no named node, or the table has no self restriction for a role of an edge that a merge into a tree parent turns into loops. The model of a complete forest, and with it the exactness of true answers, is proved in Rowl.ForestModel.

Every neighbour of a node in the forest has a neighbour path with the same label, a live node having a path of its own (live_path), and every neighbour path comes from exactly one neighbour (step_of_neighbour, neighbour_of_step, corr_function, corr_tail, corr_loop); a neighbour has only one neighbour path unless it is a tree node that is no child of a named node, which the model repeats and which no maximum restriction of a named node in a complete forest counts (corr_unique, corr_third), so for a complete forest that keeps the invariant every path satisfies every entry its label satisfies, including minimum and maximum restrictions on simple roles, self restrictions, the complements of self restrictions on simple roles, and nominals and their complements, since a nominal is only on the named node of its individual, whose label also lists the nominal of its requirement (truth), and the model respects the role hierarchy, keeps its disjoint pairs, on simple roles, apart, since a common neighbour path comes from a common neighbour (model_constrained), and satisfies the TBox concept, the unfoldings, the requirements and the links (model_of_complete). satisfiable_correct: forest::satisfiable terminates; its true answers come with a model in Type of the role hierarchy where the TBox concept and every definition hold everywhere and every fact and link holds at the elements of its individuals, and its false answers rule out every such model in any universes; it gives no answer when a structure would exceed the usize range, a number restriction, the complement of a self restriction or a disjoint pair is on a role that is not simple, a restriction with a bound from new named nodes has fewer counted named neighbours than the bound, the table has no self restriction for a role of an edge that a merge into a tree parent turns into loops, or the individual of a nominal or of the complement of one has no named node. Every neighbour of a node in the forest has a neighbour path with the same label, a live node having a path of its own (live_path), and every neighbour path comes from exactly one neighbour (step_of_neighbour, neighbour_of_step, corr_function, corr_tail, corr_loop); a neighbour has only one neighbour path unless it is a tree node that is no child of a named node, which the model repeats and which no maximum restriction of a named node in a complete forest counts (corr_unique, corr_third), so for a complete forest that keeps the invariant every path satisfies every entry its label satisfies, including minimum and maximum restrictions on simple roles, self restrictions, the complements of self restrictions on simple roles, and nominals and their complements, since a nominal is only on the named node of its individual, whose label also lists the nominal of its requirement (truth), and the model respects the role hierarchy, keeps its disjoint pairs, on simple roles, apart, since a common neighbour path comes from a common neighbour (model_constrained), and satisfies the TBox concept, the unfoldings, the requirements and the links (model_of_complete). satisfiable_correct: forest::satisfiable terminates; its true answers come with a model in Type of the role hierarchy where the TBox concept and every definition hold everywhere and every fact and link holds at the elements of its individuals, and its false answers rule out every such model in any universes; it gives no answer when a structure would exceed the usize range, a number restriction, the complement of a self restriction or a disjoint pair is on a role that is not simple, a restriction with a bound from new named nodes has fewer counted named neighbours than the bound, the table has no self restriction for a role of an edge that a merge into a tree parent turns into loops, or the individual of a nominal or of the complement of one has no named node. Every neighbour of a node in the forest has a neighbour path with the same label, a live node having a path of its own (live_path), and every neighbour path comes from exactly one neighbour (step_of_neighbour, neighbour_of_step, corr_function, corr_tail, corr_loop); a neighbour has only one neighbour path unless it is a tree node that is no child of a named node, which the model repeats and which no maximum restriction of a named node in a complete forest counts (corr_unique, corr_third), so for a complete forest that keeps the invariant every path satisfies every entry its label satisfies, including minimum and maximum restrictions on simple roles, self restrictions, the complements of self restrictions on simple roles, and nominals and their complements, since a nominal is only on the named node of its individual, whose label also lists the nominal of its requirement (truth), and the model respects the role hierarchy, keeps its disjoint pairs, on simple roles, apart, since a common neighbour path comes from a common neighbour (model_constrained), and satisfies the TBox concept, the unfoldings, the requirements and the links (model_of_complete). satisfiable_correct: forest::satisfiable terminates; its true answers come with a model in Type of the role hierarchy where the TBox concept and every definition hold everywhere and every fact and link holds at the elements of its individuals, and its false answers rule out every such model in any universes; it gives no answer when a structure would exceed the usize range, a number restriction, the complement of a self restriction or a disjoint pair is on a role that is not simple, a restriction with a bound from new named nodes has fewer counted named neighbours than the bound, the table has no self restriction for a role of an edge that a merge into a tree parent turns into loops, or the individual of a nominal or of the complement of one has no named node. Every neighbour of a node in the forest has a neighbour path with the same label, a live node having a path of its own (live_path), and every neighbour path comes from exactly one neighbour (step_of_neighbour, neighbour_of_step, corr_function, corr_tail, corr_loop); a neighbour has only one neighbour path unless it is a tree node that is no child of a named node, which the model repeats and which no maximum restriction of a named node in a complete forest counts (corr_unique, corr_third), so for a complete forest that keeps the invariant every path satisfies every entry its label satisfies, including minimum and maximum restrictions on simple roles, self restrictions, the complements of self restrictions on simple roles, and nominals and their complements, since a nominal is only on the named node of its individual, whose label also lists the nominal of its requirement (truth), and the model respects the role hierarchy, keeps its disjoint pairs, on simple roles, apart, since a common neighbour path comes from a common neighbour (model_constrained), and satisfies the TBox concept, the unfoldings, the requirements and the links (model_of_complete). satisfiable_correct: forest::satisfiable terminates; its true answers come with a model in Type of the role hierarchy where the TBox concept and every definition hold everywhere and every fact and link holds at the elements of its individuals, and its false answers rule out every such model in any universes; it gives no answer when a structure would exceed the usize range, a number restriction, the complement of a self restriction or a disjoint pair is on a role that is not simple, a restriction with a bound from new named nodes has fewer counted named neighbours than the bound, the table has no self restriction for a role of an edge that a merge into a tree parent turns into loops, or the individual of a nominal or of the complement of one has no named node. requirements.requirement: Individual kind total correct for exact individual source reading
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual Functional Syntax reading of individuals and individual lists is total and has exact result/error equivalence to an independent grammar. An individual is a full or abbreviated IRI resolved through the checked prefix table or a node ID with its exact label, both under the caller's IRI limit; a missing token reports the source length and any other token its start. An individual list is the maximal individual sequence before the closing parenthesis, which is left in place, with the caller's member-count bound checked before each further member, followed by the caller's minimum length, reported as an expected individual where the list stops. The reader is proved total by well-founded recursion on the token count; every result and first error has its derivation, every derivation is the actual result, an accepted individual consumes exactly its token and a list never consumes more than it is given. ObjectOneOf, ObjectHasValue, SameIndividual, DifferentIndividuals and the class and object property assertions read their individuals here. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.
