requirements.requirement: Verified individual equalities and inequalities for the ontology queries: intern_rest_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual individual equalities and inequalities of the ontology queries (shi_ontology), proved exact. Every member of a SameIndividual or DifferentIndividuals axiom gets a node after the individuals of the assertions, with room for one more node. The members of each equality are united under one representative by relabelling: every node starts as its own representative, and uniting two nodes replaces the representative of the second by that of the first. Every representative is a node joined to its own node by a chain of equalities (the equivalence closure of the positions of members of one SameIndividual axiom), so every OWL model gives a node and its representative one element, and the members of every equality share their representative. The check for an inequality two of whose members share a representative, counting occurrences, is exact. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

Mentions lists the individuals of the nominals of a concept; the checks for nominals (nominal, definitions_nominal, facts_nominal, closure_nominal) and that the individual of every nominal of a question's facts has a node (known, facts_known) are exact. The individuals of the nominals of the TBox concept, the definitions and the class assertions get nodes after the individuals of the assertions and equalities (nominal_individuals, definition_individuals, class_individuals, assertion_individuals). The ontology queries that use them are proved in Rowl.ShiOntology.

requirements.requirement: Verified semantics of role chains: along_append
requirements.implementation_scope: Role chains r1 ∘ … ∘ rn ⊑ r and their automata (Rowl.ChainSemantics). Chained says that an interpretation relates every pair along the roles of a chain by its role; Mirrored that every chain has its mirror, the inverted roles reversed under the inverted role. A role is complex when the role of a chain is included in it (Complex). The automaton of a complex role c (Trans) goes from its initial to its final state along c directly and along every complex role strictly below c; a transitive role or a chain of two roles equivalent to c returns from the final to the initial state; every other chain whose role is equivalent to c adds a segment of states (segOf, segOf_shape): back to the final state when its first role is equivalent to c, back to the initial state when its last role is, and from the initial to the final state otherwise. In every model of the role hierarchy and the chains the automaton of c accepts only pairs related by c, and every such pair (accepts_initial, accepts_of_rel). Stage and Closure derive from the relations of an interpretation the least relations that satisfy the inclusions, the transitive roles and the chains; with mirrored chains in a closed hierarchy an inverse role relates the reversed pairs (closure_mirror), a role that no chain reaches keeps the relation of an interpretation that respects the hierarchy (stage_simple, closure_simple), and atoms that unfold as their automata require (Unfolds) lead from the initial to the final state of the automaton of a role equivalent to the derived one along every derived pair (stage_atoms), for chains of at least two roles.

requirements.requirement: Range form total correct for exact source data-range reading
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual Functional Syntax data range reading is total and has complete exact result/error equivalence. It reads one data range at a caller-supplied position: a datatype IRI, DataIntersectionOf and DataUnionOf with at least two members, DataComplementOf, DataOneOf with at least one literal, and DatatypeRestriction with a datatype IRI and at least one pair of a constraining facet IRI and its literal; read_optional_range reads the optional data range of a data number restriction (none before the closing parenthesis or at the end). Literals use the proved literal reader, the IRI limit bounding their lexical forms and datatype IRIs, and every IRI resolves its original span through the checked prefix table. Errors return the first failing step in source order with original offsets (EOF errors use the source length): at a connective keyword the nesting depth, then the opening parenthesis, then the operands in order, where each member, literal and facet follows the count check, then the two-member minimum of an intersection or union, the one-literal minimum of an enumeration or the one-facet minimum of a restriction, then the closing parenthesis. The independent grammar is a mutually recursive derivation of data ranges, connective bodies and member sequences, with literal and facet sequences. The reader is proved total by well-founded recursion on the token count; every result and first error has its derivation, and every derivation is the actual result. A successful data range consumes at least one token and returns the unchanged suffix. The meaning of data ranges belongs to the datatype map; datatype restrictions are read here and reasoned about by a later stage. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Fast Functional Syntax token selection on validated text: longest_valid_eq
requirements.implementation_scope: Fast Functional Syntax token selection on validated text: the lexer selects each token with the early-stopping matchers (longest_valid, next_terminal_valid) and runs only the matchers of terminals whose words can begin with the next code point (next_terminal_fast). The dispatch test is proved sound against the independent terminal languages: every word of every terminal begins with a code point that passes it, so a skipped terminal has no candidate endpoint and reports no match. On every suffix with a UTF-8 decoding both shortcuts are proved equal to the standard greatest selection next_terminal, and the stream proofs use those equalities, so the lexer's correctness theorems are unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Compiled regular grammars matched over continuation stacks: lang_eq
requirements.implementation_scope: Compiled regular grammars: compile turns an expression into a table of nodes whose parts come before them, and the matcher runs partial derivatives over continuation stacks of node indices, so no part of the grammar is copied while matching. An independent reading of the table gives every node a language (a part that does not come before its node, and an index outside the table, read as the empty language); compiling keeps every node's empty-word flag equal to whether its language has the empty word and gives the root the expression's language. Each matching step is proved to replace the state's language by the words that remain after the consumed code point, so matches returns exactly the derivative matcher's matches_utf8 result, including malformed UTF-8 diagnostics, and on a suffix with a UTF-8 decoding longest_valid returns exactly longest_prefix's result. A table or state that would exceed the usize range is reported as None, and validate_iri and validate_reference then answer with the derivative matcher; their statements are unchanged.

requirements.implementation_scope: Actual consistency, class satisfiability, subsumption and instance checking with data properties, the literals of every datatype of datatypes::literal_value, and data ranges of xsd:integer, xsd:decimal, xsd:string, rdf:PlainLiteral, xsd:boolean, owl:real, owl:rational and the twelve built-in subtypes of xsd:integer, with datatype restrictions of the numeric datatypes by the range facets xsd:minInclusive, xsd:maxInclusive, xsd:minExclusive and xsd:maxExclusive with numeric bounds (data_ontology), by an encoding into classes, object properties and named individuals that the SROIQ queries of shi_ontology decide: the data values become data nodes of a class D, each data property an object property from elements that are no data nodes to data nodes, each datatype in use a class with the inclusions and disjointness of the datatypes and the booleans as the two truth values, and each literal value a named data node with a pattern of bit classes that tells it apart. When a datatype restriction or a subtype of xsd:integer is in use, the bounds become cuts of the real line, each with a class, which the kernel orders by exact arithmetic (regions): the class of the first cut lies inside the reals, each cut's class inside the one before, the two cuts of a number leave only its literal value's node, and between two neighbouring cuts of different numbers the integers are none at all, or at most their number at any element along a role U above every data property's role when there are fewer of them than a capacity that bounds the counts of the data restrictions of the closure and its questions (region_axioms_spec). An OWL model lifts to a model of the encoding with its values as the data nodes (lifted_satisfies, lifted_class), and a model of the encoding gives an OWL model whose values are chosen per element from the region its classes place each data node in: the integers, decimals that are no integers, rationals that are no decimals or irrational numbers between two neighbouring cuts, strings, tagged strings and values outside every datatype, each region infinite but a bounded run of integers, which holds the element's values by the axiom on the run or by the capacity (sound_satisfies, sound_class), so that under every datatype map that is the OWL 2 map on the datatypes of datatypes::literal_value (Normative) an answer is the Direct Semantics answer (consistent_correct, class_satisfiable_correct, subsumed_correct, instance_of_correct and their prepared forms, which leave room for questions whose data restrictions count 64 values).
